subject: RFP Q: Variable-rate smoothing & true-up approach for OrionHealth
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orionhealth.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@orionhealth.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RFP: Clarification on commercial model (section 3)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP submission. Our commercial team reviewed Section 3 (pricing) and had a few clarifying questions before we include Redwood in the final shortlist. Can you confirm the following in scope for your response?

1) Variable-rate smoothing — your response references a monthly smoothing window that can average daily burst spikes into a single charge. Is the smoothing applied before or after tiered discount bands? How are refunds/credits calculated if monthly usage falls below the committed baseline?

2) True-up cadence — do you support quarter-end true-ups, or only annual true-ups? Is there an automatic invoice offset for overages when a customer purchases additional commit mid-term?

3) Multi-year discounts & rate locks — what is your approach to rate-step-downs over a 24–36 month term, and do you provide contract language for CPI-linked adjustments or fixed USD pricing?

4) Pilot / POC pricing — for a 3-month pilot up to 20M tokens with production SLA, what discounted rates and burst allowances would you provide?

5) Billing mechanics — net terms, currency, and how burst credits are shown line-item on invoices.

Attached: RFP_Section3_Commercial.xlsx (we annotated a few rows).

Would like a response by EOD Monday (11/9) so procurement can consolidate vendors. Also open to a short sync if you prefer to walk through the model.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Cloud Sourcing
OrionHealth

[Attachment: RFP_Section3_Commercial.xlsx]
From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orionhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-05T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Clarification on commercial model (section 3)

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Quick response inline and we've attached a concise commercial summary for Orion to review. If helpful I can schedule a 30-min call to run the numbers.

1) Smoothing vs bands: smoothing is performed at the invoice level before applying tiered discounts. In practice that means short-term spikes are averaged into the monthly bill, then discounting is applied against the smoothed token total. Refunds/credits: if your month-to-month smoothed usage drops below the committed baseline, credits carry forward as a pool (expires after 12 months) or can be applied toward the next invoice — see the attached PDF for examples.

2) True-up cadence: we support both quarterly and annual true-ups. For mid-term commit purchases, we apply a pro-rated true-up on the next invoice and reduce the amount owed for previously incurred overages by applying newly purchased committed units first (automatic invoice offset).

3) Multi-year discounts: standard practice is step-down discounts at 12 and 24 months; we offer fixed USD pricing for term lengths and an optional CPI-cap clause (cap and floor pre-defined). We can provide both fixed-price and CPI-linked language in the commercial annex.

4) Pilot pricing: for a 3-month pilot (20M tokens), we propose a Pilot Rate of $12 / 1k tokens (50% of our standard list gen rate), with a 5M-token burst buffer per month included. If you convert to a 12-month commit within 30 days post-pilot, the pilot spend counts toward the initial commit ladder.

5) Billing: invoices are in USD by default, Net 30, detailed line items for committed units, burst usage, smoothing credits, and any applied discounts. We provide token-level export CSVs for reconciliation.

Attachments: Redwood_Orion_Commercial_Summary_v1.pdf (summary table + worked examples).

Next steps: I'm looping in Rishi (AE) and Marissa (Sales Lead) to confirm commercial flexibility for multi-year step-downs. If the terms above look ok, I'll prepare a commercial annex and DocuSign-ready term sheet.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Liam — appreciate the quick turn. Per our internal review we refined the draft and attached a short Commercial Annex and the standard Terms Annex with two options (fixed USD and CPI-linked). Highlights below and attached worked examples.

- Commit bands: 50M / 200M / 600M tokens per 12-month period. Baseline list rates for generation: $24 / 1k tokens; pricing shown in annex reflects committed discounts (see table).
- Smoothing: monthly smoothing averages daily usage into a smoothed-month figure; smoothing is applied prior to discount band assignment. Credits for months where smoothed usage < committed baseline are accrued and available for 12 months.
- True-up cadence: quarterly or annual (customer-selectable). Mid-term commit purchases are pro-rated and applied immediately to offset overages on the next invoice.
- Pilot offer: 3-month pilot @ $12 / 1k tokens up to 20M tokens total. Includes 5M/month burst buffer and production SLA. Pilot spend will count toward first-year commit if converted within 30 days.
- Multi-year: 24- and 36-month step-down schedules available; we can provide fixed USD pricing or CPI-linked pricing (cap: +3% / floor: 0%).
- Billing: USD invoices, Net 30. Line-itemed export for raw tokens, smoothed tokens, applied credits, and discount multipliers.

Attachments: Redwood_Commercial_Terms_Annex.docx (includes redlines and suggested language), Redwood_Orion_Commercial_Summary_v1.pdf (worked examples).
